title: feat(cache): key cache entries by configured vary headers
author: usualoma

spotlights.label: The body's Before column predates v4.12.18
spotlights.why: At the base commit, addHeader wrote Vary onto the response before shouldSkipCache looked for it, so with options.vary set nothing was ever stored (the old test asserted X-Count 2). The shared single entry the body describes is the behaviour before v4.12.18; for users on the base, this PR turns caching back on.

spotlights.label: Raw header values split variants finely
spotlights.why: The key takes the request header value verbatim, so "en-US,en;q=0.9" and "en" are different entries, and a vary on Accept-Encoding or User-Agent can multiply entries per URL. Worth a line in the docs on which headers are sensible to vary on.

spotlights.label: keyGenerator keys get the headers appended again
spotlights.why: The suffix is added after options.keyGenerator runs, so a generator that already folds in Accept-Language doubles it. The body argues this only over-splits; no test covers keyGenerator together with vary.

spotlights.label: Missing and empty header share one key
spotlights.why: A missing header becomes "" via ?? '', so a request with no Accept-Language and one with an empty Accept-Language hit the same entry. Probably harmless, but it is not what the test name "missing and present ... separate" might suggest.

spotlights.label: Merged Vary header is no longer sorted
spotlights.why: The old addHeader lowercased, deduplicated and sorted the merged list. The new one keeps configured names first, then the response's, in insertion order, so the header text can change for apps that set both.

spotlights.label: Tests use a Map, not a real Cache API
spotlights.why: The new tests stub caches with a Map keyed by the string. Whether every runtime accepts a key like https://host/path::accept-language=en (it is parsed as a URL) is not exercised here.

steps.title: Skip caching only when the response varies on unconfigured headers
steps.why: parseVaryDirectives turns a Vary value or the vary option into trimmed lowercase names. shouldSkipCache now skips a response with Vary only if some name is outside options.vary, and the call site parses the response Vary before addHeader adds the configured names.
steps.consequence: A response with no Vary, or one covered by options.vary, can be stored again; Vary: * and uncovered names still skip, as do private/no-store and Set-Cookie.

notes: Only a Vary the handler set counts
Old check saw the added Vary: always skipped

steps.title: Key each entry by the configured request header values
steps.why: options.vary is parsed once into a Set of lowercase names (undefined when empty). After the URL or keyGenerator key, the middleware appends ::name=value for each configured header, URL-encoded.
steps.consequence: Requests that differ in a configured header read and write different cache entries, so a stored variant is only served to a matching request.

notes: Adds the configured request headers to the cache key variants
const varyDirectives = optionsVaryList.length ? new Set(optionsVaryList) : undefined

steps.title: Build the response Vary header from the parsed lists
steps.why: addHeader now receives the parsed response Vary. With none, it writes the configured names; otherwise it merges both sets and writes * if either contains it.
steps.consequence: Clients still see every configured header in Vary, and the header no longer has to be re-split inside addHeader.

steps.title: Prove variants, misses and the remaining skips
steps.why: A store-backed cache stub replaces the spy for the new cases. The old "not cache" test flips to expect a hit, and new tests cover per-language variants, a missing header, two configured headers, a covered handler Vary, an uncovered Cookie and Vary: *.
steps.consequence: Each row of the body's behaviour table has a test, against a Map stand-in rather than a runtime cache.
